utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning, everyone. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Excellencies. Good morning to everyone. Good morning, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 12 of your report, you said: [In English] "None of the SFRY federal, republic or provincial documents examined to date use the term 'Crisis Staff' or 'War Presidency,' although the latter term is found in the 1984 Statute of the Prijedor municipality." [Interpretation] And in paragraph 13, you say: [In English] "As noted above, the term, itself, has not been found in any legislation. The SDS used this undefined term and applied it to a different kind of body, a party organ which claimed the authority of a collective municipal presidency." [Interpretation] You put that in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is in my report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see D368 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We're waiting for the English version, but you know the Serbian language and you can look at it already. Is it a document from the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, dated September 21, 1991?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 31st -- at the 31st session of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Then we see who was present; the president, Izetbegovic, Plavsic, Kljuic, Boras and Ejub Ganic, including also the president from -- member of the SFRY Presidency, Bogicevic, Prime Minister Jure Pelivan, Cengic, Jerko Doko, Alija Delimustafic, the general secretary and his deputy. At this meeting, on page 2 in Serbian and English -- could we see page 2. Let us look at this: "The Presidency established the Crisis Staff with the following composition: Members of the Presidency, Ejub Ganic; co-ordinator, Dr. Biljana Plavsic; Franjo Boras; Minister of the Interior, Delimustafic; Defence Minister Jerko Doko, and the commander of the Territorial Defence. "The base of the Crisis Staff will be at the premises of the Presidency ..." On what basis was this Crisis Staff established?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a citation to legislation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the SDS make this up and set this up, as you suggest in paragraph 13, that the SDS is using this undefined term, or is it the state presidency, the presidency of the republic, that established this?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I note in footnote 5, there were other crisis staffs. Had I understood -- this issue has come up before in earlier times that I'm testifying, and if I understood it was such a difficult issue for the other side, I would have expanded it. There were other crisis staffs. I do not claim that the SDS invented the term. What I do state is I have not found any legislation using that term. And because it is used from the level of the Presidency to the level of a factory, I consider it a fairly undefined, flexible, ad-hoc term. So, yes, we see a crisis staff here in the BH Presidency. We will see other crisis staffs formed elsewhere. What I do not find is a legislative definition of the term "crisis staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So your first -- the first sentence in para 12 is not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not found -- oh, documents, yes. I'm sorry, the "documents" is not correct. Yes, I see the problem there, and I apologise for that. It should be "legislation." Indeed, that is wrong, misleading, and I understand now the source of the misunderstanding here. So I will readily agree we see documents about other crisis staffs. I don't find legislation on it, and my apologies for that error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1990 or 1991, OSCE formed a crisis staff to monitor the situation in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why did you put all the rest in your footnote and you included only the SDS in paragraph 13 and ascribe this invention to the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not ascribe it as an invention of the SDS. My terms of reference were to examine the Bosnian Serb crisis staffs. Therefore, that's the thrust of my writing. However, I note that there are other crisis staffs. I will readily concede that there were crisis staffs on the Bosnian side and on the Croat side. It doesn't affect my conclusions about Bosnian Serb crisis staffs, which I see as formed on the orders of the SDS. I do not say the SDS invented the term. I say that the SDS ordered the formation of SDS party crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And your main task was to study the legislative origins and legislative grounds of crisis staffs relative to which legal system?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legislative origins was part of my task. My tasking was the origins and operations of Bosnian Serb crisis staffs, not the legislative origins of the term "crisis staff," per se. Obviously, I would look at the legal system which was in place at the time that the crisis staffs were formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it right that in the letter of 16 December 2009, sent to you by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, you were primarily tasked with studying the legislative basis for crisis staffs or not? If it's listed as the first task, isn't it then your primary job?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I see that as a kind of chronological ordering of the topics to be studied. I don't think that it's more important than the role of the crisis staffs in the Bosnian Serb state or the actions of the crisis staffs in the municipalities. I see all those topics as having equal weight, and I think she arranged them in a logical progression.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, you were supposed to find the legal basis in our legal system. Is it possible you don't know that there are legal grounds in our laws to form various bodies, including the operation of municipal authorities in municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I would look for the legal basis in the legal system operating at the time the crisis staffs were formed. I do note that there is certainly provision in the legislation for collective municipal presidencies to operate in time of emergency. I want to stress, I do not see these named as crisis staffs. I would be very glad to find some legislation that uses the term "crisis staff," because it's so widely used I'm surprised that it doesn't appear. But I do see legislation for collective municipal authorities and also for the councils for all people's defence. I note these in my report. But I repeat, I find no legislation for crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember a provision which provides for the collective municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I note that in the first paragraph, "the Presidency." It's known as the Presidency, not as the War Presidency, but it's in the -- I found it in the Bosnian Constitution. I believe it's also in the SFRY Constitution, but I thought this was enough of a citation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you note it in your footnotes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Footnote 1. Paragraph 11 deals with this concept of a collective municipal presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you also state this example of the Crisis Staff formed by the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina as something unusual and illegal, not based in law?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that crisis staffs, in themselves, are illegal. I say they are not legally defined. That's the difference, not to say crisis staffs, as a notion, are illegal. But, no, I did not cite this Presidency Crisis Staff in my report on Bosnian Serb municipal crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we see 1D3563.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: If they are not legally defined, what, then, is their status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: If they are not legally defined, what is their status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I find that hard to define. I think their authority is what they claim. That's my -- how I see it. I think in the example of this kind of crisis staff formed at the Presidency, it's meant to be kind of a maybe a working group or a special-tasked group, the centre for information, where information is supposed to go, the people who need to deal with it most quickly and effectively. But it's formed within the body here of the Presidency and has, I think, the authority of the Presidency. It's all Presidency members who form the Crisis Staff. As I say, I have not found any legislation on it. I have heard some discussion of it as just a term that would be used even in a factory. If there is, you know, a flood in the municipality, the municipality might form a crisis staff of the most important actors in the municipality to solve problems. The Socialist system had a tradition of collective self-management. A group get together of -- to act collectively, and in this case, a small group in times of emergency, but I can't say what its status was. It seems to be whatever people wanted to be at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see that Professor Koljevic was not a member of the Crisis Staff, so that not all members of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina were in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean all members were. I said it's a smaller group. But those who are, as far as I can see, are members of the Presidency or else people who, ex officio, ought to be involved. No, I do not see that Koljevic is a member of the Presidency -- I'm sorry, of the Crisis Staff. He is certainly a member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it the case that in municipal crisis staffs, members were chosen ex officio to do jobs they normally did?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the crisis staffs that I looked at, the Bosnian Serb crisis staffs, they were first formed within the party, and they had party members who were either already performing municipal functions or were the unsuccessful SDS candidates for those functions, so they would not include the non-Serb municipal president, president of Executive Board, other positions. So it was not a question of taking everybody in the municipal positions, but those Serbs -- SDS members who either fulfilled those positions or were chosen by the SDS as candidates for those positions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll come back to that. Can we see 1D3563.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this is a document of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated 18 September 1991, and it says they made certain conclusions; namely, that the hitherto Security Council shall from now on be called the Crisis Staff of the BH HDZ and shall consist of the following people: Stjepan Kljuic, Mate Boban, Branko Kvesic, who was chief of the joint security, Mijo Tokic, Jerko Djoko, minister of the Joint Defence, and other people, including Bozo Rajic, who was assistant minister: "Alongside the Executive Political Crisis Staff, the Staff shall set up a specialist command organ which will be the expert military organ with direct responsibility for individual operative areas. "The Crisis Staff shall start working immediately and shall be in charge of the entire system of the defence of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina and ensure the acquisition of weapons. "The president of the Crisis Staff shall be Stjepan Kljuic, and the vice-president, Mate Boban." Have you reviewed this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it before. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see here that before this Crisis Staff, they had a security council, whereas Serbs formed one only on the 27th of March, 1992. They had a crisis staff several months before the Serbs. They had an executive police organ. They had a military organ, a specialised one. The president of the Crisis Staff was the president of the HDZ and member of the Presidency, Stjepan Kljuic. And you relegated this to a footnote?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a footnote in my report on the Bosnian Serb municipal crisis staffs -- or not this document, itself, is a footnote, but the existence of other crisis staffs. I don't cite this document, itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this conduct of this party in our political life of any influence to the conduct of the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possibly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see what the Crisis Staff is supposed to do. It must convene meetings at the request of any member. The second paragraph: "In the event of armed conflicts in areas dominated by Croatian population, crisis staffs shall assume all the functions of municipal authorities, and it shall continue until the threat of war ceases. Crisis staffs must also be established urgently along these same lines as the republican and regional crisis staffs: The Travnik regional community, Herzegovina regional community, and the Posavina regional community. "The Republican Crisis Staff shall co-ordinate the Sarajevo regional community of the BH HDZ directly." And item 3, second paragraph, says: "It is recommended that the chairpersons of the municipal crisis staffs should be the presidents of the municipalities if they were appointed by the HDZ, and if not, the presidents of the municipal executive councils or the chairmen of the municipal boards of the BH HDZ. "It is the duty of the persons representing the BH HDZ in the government bodies to continue performing their tasks conscientiously --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can all read the document. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: Did you cite this document, even if only in a footnote, as an example of early establishment of HDZ crisis staff, including all the Croatian representatives in the BH authorities, including the political and military command component, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, I did not cite this document in my report on Bosnian Serb municipal crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, look at this, what Kljuic is doing; contact the SDA, ask them to make their political position clear, but he's also duty-bound to elaborate their own political position, even without the co-operation of the SDA. And look at item 9: "The regional and municipal crisis staffs are tasked with urgently establishing a system of information and alerting in emergency conditions." And the last page: "Note: This material and instructions are strictly confidential and may be made available only to the members of the Security Council of the BH HDZ, members of the Presidency from the HDZ, and presidents of municipal boards." Would the council be completely informed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Would the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- be fully informed about the nature of the Serbian crisis staffs if this is kept away from them?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had been tasked to discuss all crisis staffs in Bosnia at the beginning of the conflict, yes, I would have included this. I do not see that the existence of other crisis staffs changes my conclusions about how the Bosnian Serb municipal crisis staffs were formed. And my tasking was the Bosnian Serb municipal crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you mean to say that intensive preparations for the war on the part of the Croat and Muslim sides in Bosnia and Herzegovina throughout 1991 did not have any influence over the fact that the Serb side activated their crisis staffs not earlier than April 1992, and that actions of the Serb side were unjustified, unmotivated, that it happened in a vacuum, so it was an act of diversion on the part of the Serb side; sabotage, in other words?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not claim that the actions of the Serb side were unjustified, unmotivated. I do not even claim that events happened in a vacuum. However, I am not called as an historical expert. I was not asked to discuss the entire origins of the conflict in Bosnia. So although I think the Trial Chamber should be, certainly, made aware of the events in 1991, I do not see that as my specific job here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1329, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D3569.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, Remzo Tucakovic from Novi Grad explains -- please look at item 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I don't see a translation for that document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this not the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It seems to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Remzo Tucakovic is writing to the Main Board of the SDA, and in item 2, he says as follows: "At the multi-party elections, after the formation of the SDA, I joined the party and immediately made myself available to organise the military wing of the party, the Patriotic League ..." And then further down in the same paragraph, he says: "When the Patriotic League was organised in the beginning of 1991, I was elected to the Crisis Staff of Novi Grad municipality, and I worked on forming the first Patriotic League units." Can we go on to the next page in the English language: " ... which is to take over the defence of the Miro Popara local commune, Vojnicko Polje, and then arming them." "After the formation of these Patriotic League units, I began to train them ..." "I did the same with all Patriotic League units ..." And so on. And then further on he says: "When the war began, we were quite ready to offer armed resistance and successfully resist the aggression. I successfully carried out all of the tasks," and so on, "assigned by the crisis staff of Novi Grad municipality." So he explains what he actually did and explains the whole situation. I don't want to read everything. But have you considered this document at all, have you taken it into account? And the fact that as early as in 1991, there was a crisis staff which was active, setting up a secret military organisation called the Patriotic League, does it mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the term "crisis staff" was used by a number of different bodies. As I said, I have seen other crisis staffs. My tasking was Bosnian Serb municipal crisis staffs. I don't see this one as a Bosnian Serb crisis staff. It is municipal, but it seems to be an SDA organ, not the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when you spoke about the Crisis Staff -- the Serb Crisis Staff of Novi Grad, did you take into account the fact that the SDA Crisis Staff had already been in existence for a year before the Serb Crisis Staff was established, and that the Patriotic League unit was already in existence, that it was already trained and armed and so on? Because this man describes precisely what he did to that effect.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because my tasking was not to describe the -- all events of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So although it was your task to present a full report in order to enable the Trial Chamber and the laypeople to understand what was happening, what the Serbs did, you left out all the context -- the entire context in which the Serbs were acting. You isolated the Serbs, and then you said that in April 1992, they started setting up their crisis staffs. Is this, indeed, a full report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has said on a number of occasions what the terms of reference were for writing the report. I think it's been asked and answered. And it's not for Mr. Karadzic to say that it's her task to present a full report in order to enable the Trial Chamber and the laypeople to understand what was happening. She's already explained what she did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree, Ms. Sutherland. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, again it's a comment in the guise of a question, and it's not helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellencies, I merely paraphrased what is contained in the letter of the 6th of December, written by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. I will read it: [In English] "In relation to the admission into evidence of source material used by an expert in compiling his or her report, the Chamber notes that the purpose of having an expert report is to assist the Chamber by providing an understandable compilation and analysis of technical materials which might not easily be comprehensible by a layperson. Expert reports, generally, should be complete and understandable in themselves, such that there is no need to tender for admission into evidence the sources used by an expert in compiling his or her reports." [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, we have a Prosecution person testifying here, not an unbiased, independent expert, and that's my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall having received this letter, and do you remember that Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff informed you about the position of the Trial Chamber in this matter?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me if I received that letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you. This is a letter to you: "Dear Ms. Hanson," dated the 16th of December, 2009. And let me repeat, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff repeats several times that this is the position of the Trial Chamber, that your report should be comprehensible and comprehensive and full, and you act selectively and you single out the Serb side, you isolate it, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you're commencing an argumentative line with the witness. It's not helpful. If you are going to make a reasoned comment later on that the witness's evidence is partial, that's entirely a matter for you. But at the moment, it would be much wiser to use the limited time available to ask specific and pointed questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Morrison. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of this letter?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall it at the moment, I'm afraid, but I see my -- the terms of reference letter. I'm sure I saw it, but I can't recall it. I'm not aware of it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the letter? Is it in e-court? Otherwise, let's put it on the ELMO so that we can have a look.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we zoom in a bit further so that we can read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Having heard the question from Mr. Karadzic, could you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this document. It was a request to provide a list of source documents to accompany my report, which eventually formed the basis of Annex A and Annex B. It's after my report has been written. It's to make a selection of the documents best shown to the Court, the most illustrative documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this letter please be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1330, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like this letter by Ms. Hanson to everybody in the Prosecution to also be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you notified the Prosecution that you found as follows: [In English] "At the joint meeting of the Crisis Staff and the Trnovo SDS Main Command, a decision was passed that the entire Serb population of Trnovo from the territory of Sirokari, Dobro Polje And Kalinovik be evacuated by 30th of May 1992 and that in a joint effort with the Kalinovik forces, the entire Muslim and other population be killed or expelled in an armed intervention to thus provide an ethnically clean Serb territory along the entire line of Krupac-Foca." [Interpretation] Did you write this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this email relates to the report that Ms. Hanson wrote for the Krajisnik case, not the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's immaterial. This is a document, a letter, about the fact that a document was discovered, and Ms. Hanson recommends that this document be used by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your letter?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe you also have the following letter in which I say why I don't want to use this document, because it turns out not to have been what I -- not reliable.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we will move on to the next letter now, but can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have a date? Yes, that can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1331, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the letter that follows the one that we've just seen, the one that you mentioned, and you say: "Dear all. [In English] "I should have been more skeptical about the Trnovo Territorial Defence document I sent around last week; it was, of course, too good to be true." [Interpretation] And then you go on to explain that this was, in fact, a document -- the previous document was a document produced by the Muslim Secret service. Why is it, then, too good to be true, Madam?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they interpreted this -- what they said about the ethnically-clean Serbian territory was not in the originally-sourced material. I had found two summaries of -- typewritten summaries of the handwritten minutes of the Trnovo SDS and Crisis Staff. The transcriptions of the minutes were accurate, but I found -- so I had assumed they were reliable. When I found that these summaries were, in fact, too good to be true, I looked at them more closely and saw that they were not the original documents, so I withdrew them from my report. I went back and withdrew all typewritten transcriptions of the minutes, and I used the original handwritten minutes myself. So I do not use this document in my report. I rely only on the handwritten original minutes. Usually, an analyst knows if a document is too good to be true, it's probably not true. The trial was ongoing. We were looking for -- we were looking for exhibits. This caught my eye. Within a few days, I caught my mistake. I corrected it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, I am challenging your impartiality here, because you are sad because a document that is harmful to the Serbs is not authentic, so you're looking for the Serbs' wrongdoings. You are -- you feel sorry that this document is not authentic, because you wanted to catch the Serbs red-handed planning the ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was -- I --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like my question to be interpreted, because I asked: "Is that right?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In addition to writing an expert report, I generally assisted the Krajisnik -- brought to the attention of the trial team evidence. The team was prosecuting a Bosnian Serb leader. "Too good to be true" is just generally a phrase analysts use, like "a smoking gun," but -- no, not "a smoking gun," but something that's "too good to be true" is just the sort of thing we're looking for, but fits so nicely with what we need that we have to be more skeptical about it. And I was, in the first few days, skeptical about it. And I said I didn't use it in my report, it's not in my presentation, so I don't think my conclusions are harmed. Had I been assigned to a team prosecuting Croat perpetrators or Bosnian Muslim perpetrators, I would doing my professional best to assist the Prosecution in those endeavours, and I would be looking for evidence that supported that. I would also be looking for exculpatory evidence and bringing it to the attention of the trial team. I don't see that finding a document which summarises the case nicely, and then saying, Oops, it's not reliable, is an example of bias.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you are assisting the Prosecution, and you are looking for something that fits in, that dovetails in the case. So what does it fit in; the presumption of the Serbs' guilt? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs, you mean all Serbs? I certainly don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, Madam.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand your question. I am looking for evidence that supports the Prosecution case. I am also looking at all the evidence to see where the Prosecution case is incorrect, or needs to be corrected, or the Prosecution doesn't understand things. This, as I said, dates from the time of the Krajisnik trial, when I was not kept at a distance. For this trial, I have not been involved in any of the Prosecution theory, or team meetings, or looking for evidence beyond my report. I want to stress that, because it was a different modus operandi back at the time of this e-mail. For the purposes of this trial, my participation was limited to my report and the evidence that I've been looking for for my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you studied the indictment in the Krajisnik case, and then you sought to underpin it, to support it. Ms. Hanson, thank you very much for your answer. And I would like this document to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You made a statement without asking a question. That does not help the Trial Chamber, Mr. Karadzic. Do you like to comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, a little while ago, you said that you looked for documents that support the indictment; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But, again, there's no question, Your Honour. "Is that so" on the end of it as I rose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, there's a question. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we have a problem with interpretation, because I started my question by saying -- by an inversion, "Did you," and that was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time of the e-mail, I had written my report but was still pulling up documents I would like to use in my court presentation. That is the context of that thing. In the Krajisnik case, once my testimony was over, I was fully participating in the Prosecution team. Again, I did not base my report on the indictment. I was given a tasking very early on, Would you look at crisis staffs? We don't know what these bodies were. Were they rogue organs, were they part of the state? What were they doing? That was my general first tasking. I wrote a memo -- an internal memo on that, which the Prosecution team then suggested I turn into an expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit this second e-mail.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1332, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By the way, did we deal with 1D3569? Are you tendering that? Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would object. It's the Chamber's practice not to admit statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's attached to a document. Can we see the document, 1D3569. Can we see the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a report to the Main Board of the Democratic Action Party. It's not a statement; it's a report. It's, in fact, a complaint about the decision on promotion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So it's a form of a statement, Your Honour. It's a complaint about non-promotion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to reply, Mr. Robinson, on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I don't believe that I have anything to add at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this document, not for the whole truth of the document, but the fact that in this letter, a certain individual is referring to a crisis staff. It will be admitted. So to that extent, we'll admit this document. And give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1333, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have 65 ter 512.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 512, here we have the Croatian Democratic Union of the Kotor Varos Municipality, the Municipal Board. The date is the 16th of March, 1992. It's the decision on the establishment of the Crisis Staff, with the following members. Did you include this document in your report when you wrote about Kotor Varos municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not include this in my report on Bosnian Serb municipal crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1334, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now let us go back to Bosanski Petrovac, which you describe as a municipality where there was persecution. Can I please have 65 ter 1074. These are minutes from a session of the Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we move on, I wanted to check that while Ms. Hanson refers to Bosanski Petrovac and Kotor Varos, they are not included in the indictment. Is that correct, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, they were --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were removed. They were in the indictment. However, this is not relevant to the municipality. It's relevant to the report. Ms. Hanson says the crisis staffs were responsible of wrong-doing there. We can't take her word for it. We have to see the documents on the basis of which she made that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding is Ms. Hanson wrote a report before those parts were removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it's updated, the report has been updated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In September. I'm not limiting you. I just asked that for the information. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at this: "Dragan Gacesa ..." that's the third paragraph: "Dragan Gacesa, chief of the Public Security Station, informed those present on the operation of disarmament in the territory of the municipality. He said the leaders of the SDA will appeal to their population to surrender weapons in one location and that they will bring it to the Public Security Station." Can we see page 2. Do you see that leads of the SDA, on the 13th of June, are active, and they are involved in disarming their own supporters?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at the conclusions. Item 6: "The Public Security Station is hereby ordered to disarm Zeljko Topalovic, Mica Zec from Bjelaj and Basta, Milan from Krnjeusa." Since you know our language and those times and circumstances, do you agree that these three persons were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: These three people certainly appear to be Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1335, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 65 ter 1075. A crisis staff session on the 1st of June, 1992. We can read the entire, but we have no time. Could we see page 2, item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At this session, the Crisis Staff reviewed the situation in the territory of Petrovac municipality, specifically the issue of certain representatives of the SDA moving out: "The Crisis Staff concluded that the best solution for the moment is that the said representatives remain in Petrovac and that they are now what their people need the most." Were you aware of this document of the Petrovac Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I reviewed the documents of the Petrovac Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And on this basis, you concluded the Serbs were conducting ethnic cleansing; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five days later, Petrovac was one of the municipalities that said that they wanted Muslims to move out to a level at which Serb power can be efficiently maintained in their territory. As I noted yesterday, Petrovac was one of the most Serbian of any of the municipalities, and the Muslims were largely contained within the city. I believe that most Muslims in the municipality lived within the city of Bosanski Petrovac, and perhaps -- my conclusion would be that perhaps it was not difficult to maintain Serbian power over that territory, given the specific situations in Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, the document you are referring to was not signed, whereas here you have an official document, according to protocol, signed properly, and still you do not attach due attention to it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I attach the attention to it that it deserves. I have seen another -- other documents which confirm the sub-region meeting and other documents from Sanski Most Crisis Staff which echo the ideas in the sub-region meeting that I do find that one credible. As I say, I don't find them incompatible here. The municipality wants Muslims to move out to a level at which Serbian power can be maintained efficiently. Petrovac was in such a situation already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is not true, Madam, and we will prove it. But why did you not cite this at least as the initial position of the authorities in Petrovac? Why didn't you mention that the authorities in Petrovac tried to keep the leadership of the SDA so that they would be able to solve the problems of their own community?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we see in the course of the summer, the main problem --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am asking you about this initial position, the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you ask a question, you do not intervene while the witness answers your question. It's unacceptable. Please proceed, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the course of the summer, we see that one of the principal concerns of the Muslims of Petrovac is their safety in remaining and the organised moving out of the Muslims. Therefore, this is not incompatible, to say that the leaders of the people should stay now with the Muslims that there are in Petrovac. Perhaps one possible interpretation is they want them there to help keep order. We saw that they were helping hand over -- helping the Muslims hand over their weapons. The Serb leadership may have found it useful to have those leaders there to help manage the Muslims that were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question was whether you reflected such observation in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my report, I can -- I put the documents in context of all the events over the -- over the course of the critical months. I would weigh this against what we do know about the organised moving out of Muslims, what we do know about the population structure of Petrovac. So, no, this specific document I don't have in my report, and I explained why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hanson. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I would appreciate it if you would refrain from speculating and judging. I asked you if you acknowledged this initial effort to provide security to the Muslims and cited this document, and you said, no, you did not even notice these initial efforts in the beginning of June to give safety to the Muslims, and you made a judgement that it is not important.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, it's comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, and then that's the question asked and answered. We'll give the number for this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'll just note, Your Honour, that it's a Crisis Staff meeting held on the 29th of May, 1992. The document is dated the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1336, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will now go through this summer that you refer to and see the development of events. Can we now see 65 ter 7024.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are minutes of the 3rd June, and the session was on the 2nd of June. And item 1 says it was decided that all Muslims and Croats who wish to evacuate from the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina should be enabled do so, and it's based on the conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina that all Muslims and Croats who so wish be enabled to evacuate from the territory, but only under the condition that the Serbs outside the Serbian autonomous regions also be allowed to evacuate to the territory of the Serbian Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And then the next page in English, second paragraph: "From Central Bosnia, a large number of Serbs want to move to Krajina, but the local authorities do not let them. They keep them as sort of hostages." "The Crisis Staff simultaneously decided to put up resistance to all attempts to forcibly move the population and to stop this by all legal means." Do you know that in this case, the Crisis Staff limits itself to voluntary movement of population and sets the condition that it must be reciprocal?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take that to be the ARK Crisis Staff, not the Petrovac Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, the Petrovac Crisis Staff received this. Bogdan Latinovic read out the conclusion of the Crisis Staff of Krajina, and this Crisis Staff, on that basis, makes its own decision and its own option; to enable voluntary evacuation on the condition that the Serbs are allowed to do the same. And then it says the Crisis Staff will resolutely oppose forcible movement of population or anyone moving out under pressure. Did you take this document into account? --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed this document. I did not include it in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First resolve this, whether this is an ARK crisis or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's ambiguous. It's ambiguous. They are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the first page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are discussing the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff under item 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it says -- the heading says "Municipal Assembly, Petrovac Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but on the agenda -- item 1 on the agenda is discussing the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff. So then under agenda item 1, they are proposing to adopt in full the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff, but it's not clear if -- whose conclusions they are. If we go on to the English on the next page, it seems to be the conclusions adopted in full I would read to be the ARK Crisis Staff conclusions. In the paragraph -- in reaching this kind of decision, it's clearly referring to the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. If you read AD-1, a certain individual read the conclusion of the Banja Luka Crisis Staff, and Petrovac Municipality Crisis Staff gave a proposition to be adopted in full as follows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. So I'm just saying the last two paragraphs are ambiguous as to just which crisis staff, but certainly it states here -- if they are adopting it in full, they are adopting, yes, the -- the conclusion to oppose any kind of forceful evacuation of the population. So perhaps it's not a difference. It was just -- I have -- I've reviewed all the minutes of the Petrovac Crisis Staff, so I've read this at some point. But just to be presented with it right now, it took a moment to sort out which crisis staff. I apologise if it seems a waste of time, but I had to sort it out. They seem to be adopting the ARK position, but at the same time we know what happened in the ARK and what was going on in the ARK at this time. So this document has to be weighed against the actual events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to say, if I could assist Ms. Hanson and the Court, the ARK conclusion is in an exhibit, and we could actually put them side by side. There seems to me -- it appears there is text -- the second-to-last paragraph on the document that we see on the screen doesn't appear to be in the ARK Crisis Staff conclusion, but I don't know if you want to bring up this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It may be the subject of your redirect, but let's proceed. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you then look at the last page: "The Crisis Staff invites the leadership of the SDA and HDZ to actively get involved in enabling the movement of population." Can we see the last page -- the second page in both versions with conclusions, the passage before the conclusions. Item 5 says: "The Crisis Staff decides that a board be appointed to implement these conclusions, conclusions about the evacuation of Muslims from the territory of the municipality."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot follow at this speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you slow down and repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page in English. Yes, that's it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 5, second paragraph: "The Crisis Staff has decided to form a board for the implementation of these conclusions; that is to say, the evacuation of Muslims from the territory of Petrovac municipality." The following persons were appointed to the board: Safet Hidic, Rifet Bahtijaragic, Dragan Ivanic, Slavko Banjac. Do you agree that the first two names are Muslims and the second two names are Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit D1337.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1091, please. 1091. Am I mispronouncing things so that interpreters do not understand me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is also minutes from the 14th of July. I don't want to read everything. Let's look at AD-1: "Introductory statement. To take position at the level of the Autonomous Region of Krajina as to how to treat the population which is not loyal to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The loyal part of the population should be involved in defence preparations, such as building fortifications, construction and repair of roads for logistical support and so on, in view of the fact that currently there were not enough weapons to arm these people, too, and send them to the front." I invite the interpreters to use what is on the screen. And then the next paragraph -- the next page in English: "Furthermore, D. Gacesa informed those present that some business premises owned by citizens of Muslim nationality had been damaged the previous night by bomb or mine explosions, and a vigorous investigation was underway to find the perpetrators." Were you aware the authorities in Petrovac were not destroying Muslim businesses, but instead were looking for the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, they are not destroying Muslim businesses. I know in other ones, they are closing Muslim businesses. The very fact is they are making that distinction between Muslim businesses and Serb-owned businesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that and we'll see why, although it was your duty to present that here. Let us have page 2, please, in Serbian. The English page is good. Then it's 3. This is just the certification? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Obrad Vrzina stressed the demand that all Muslims working in administration of the Municipal Assembly be sent on unpaid leave to diffuse the dissatisfaction among citizens and TO members over the fact that Muslims were receiving salaries, while a large number of citizens and TO members had no income whatsoever as a result of war operations." And further down, Bogdan Latinovic says in the last sentence: "But also there are some Muslim officials who are still working very hard in responsible jobs, and their abrupt removal from their jobs would have adverse consequences on the functioning of administrative organs." And in the conclusions, it says: "The work of --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We don't have a reference. This is going too fast. It doesn't lend itself to simultaneous interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Start from the conclusion. The interpreters simply cannot catch up with your speed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters, but I'm under time pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here in the conclusions, the last paragraph -- that is, the first paragraph, last sentence, they are wondering how to treat the Muslims, Muslim citizens, who did not declare their loyalty or who made their hostility clear. And Bogdan Latinovic says that Muslim officials and employees who are working well in the municipality should not be removed. Do you agree, Ms. Hanson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, could Mr. Karadzic refrain from stating what's not in the document in his comments and questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic? Could you reformulate your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question, Ms. Hanson: Do you see that here, Muslim officials, in the middle of June, two and a half months into the war, are still working, receiving their salaries, and under the circumstances of civil war, there are many people who are unhappy about it, and the municipality is wondering what to do, and an experienced, politically mature man, such as Latinovic, is opposed to the idea of sending them on leave?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reference here to know about his political maturity, but I see the conclusion is that they refer to the ARK because they find it, apparently, a difficult question, but they will prepare a plan for excluding employees of Muslim nationality and prepare replacements of Serbian nationality. That's what the document says. They're discussing it. The very fact that they're discussing whether some of their citizens should be allowed to continue in employment tells you what it meant; to create a Serb power in a mixed municipality, even one that I say is one of the most Serbian municipalities. The few Muslims that are there are still working. Some people don't like that. They're going to prepare a plan to replace them with Serbs, but there are referring it to the ARK because the ARK has made statements that Muslims should not be in any leading positions. The ARK has made it clear that Muslims should not be employed in significant places. Latinovic's political experience and maturity, as you say, may be in avoiding making a decision and referring it up to a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, do you accept that they are doing that under pressure, the pressure of dissatisfied masses who are not getting paid and who have to go to the front-line?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that that is -- one member is saying that that's the reason. I also know that the ARK was taking a similar position from above.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now dealing with Petrovac. I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Petrovac was part of ARK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted. Exhibit D1338. And we'll have a break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. Karadzic, Judge Baird has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, before the break, in answering one of the questions put to you by Dr. Karadzic, you stated, inter alia, that had you been assigned to a team prosecuting Croat perpetrators or Bosnian Muslim perpetrators, you would have done your professional best to assist the Prosecution in those endeavours. And this is my focus: And you would also be looking for exculpatory evidence and bringing it to the attention of the trial team. Do you recollect this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes, all right. And, indeed, I think on the first day you testified, you had stated that in respect of your present report, when you encountered exculpatory evidence, you passed it on to the lawyers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, what I would like you to assist us with, Ms. Hanson, is: What was the impediment, if there was one, to your including that exculpatory evidence in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I don't see the -- in the issue of some Muslims wanting to leave, I don't see that as exculpatory to the forced removal of those who didn't want to leave or to the creation of conditions such that people felt they had no choice but to leave their homes. I would say exculpatory would be rather stating, We see that some of our citizens want to leave. That's not the kind of state we want. Let's do everything we can to make them stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Did you encounter any exculpatory material at all in preparing this report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I encountered much exculpatory material, beyond even the scope of crisis staffs, not a lot, but I'm saying beyond the question of what crisis staffs did or didn't. That's part of my job as review of other documents. In terms of the crisis staffs, itself, yes, I did encounter a few. I passed them on. But the terms of my -- the understanding -- my understanding of exculpatory material was that evidence that would show that some other -- somebody else or some other organs committed crimes -- the crimes ascribed, not that the other side also committed crimes, for example. And my report -- in my report, I do not try to pass judgement. I simply state what I saw going on. So a municipality in which a crisis staff or war presidency is acting like a regular municipal authority and caring for its people would be what one would expect a municipal authority to do. It's when I see them doing something that fits into the overall pattern of the crimes in Bosnia in 1992, then I would fit it into those crimes. Do you understand? Am I being clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I thank you, I thank you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, you referred to the creation of conditions such that people felt that they had no choice but to leave their homes. Was that also part of your mandate as an expert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As an expert, I'm expected to know the overall events. I was not tasked to present them in the report, but I was certainly expected to know what was going on in Bosnia at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, what purpose would it serve, that you knew something, if unless you include it in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't include everything I know in one report, but it informs -- my reading of documents, it informs my interpretation of documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at 65 ter 1163.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You've just said that the Serbs -- or, rather, the authorities in Bosanski Petrovac treated buildings owned by Muslims differently, and I'm here referring to various businesses, cafes, and shops and so on. This is the -- probably the document that you're referring to. It says here that: "Muslim owners or keepers of catering establishments and businesses shall close their premises for their own security and that of their property. "The closing of premises is of a temporary nature ." The date is the 18th of June, 1992. Is this the document that you had in mind, or perhaps you had some other document in mind?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the one I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1339, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 1093. Your Excellencies, while we're waiting for this document to come up, I would kindly ask you to give me Friday, because I would have less than three minutes to deal with each paragraph in the report and I could not even begin to address the documents. I have 420 minutes for 147 paragraphs, and I kindly ask you to give me some additional time on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You were allotted seven hours to deal with this witness for your cross-examination, and you spent hours and hours to deal with matters that took place in Petrovac and Kotor Varos. And you have an hour and a half for this session. How much more would you need at all?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, as regards Kotor Varos, Krupa, Bosanski Petrovac, they're not contained in the indictment, but they are presented here as the striking examples of the worst actions on the part of the Serb authorities. And we have documents to support that, and I need all the sessions today and all the sessions on Friday in order to be able to examine this witness on all the particulars. We're talking about 147 paragraphs in the report and thousands and thousands of documents that are referred to in the document, itself, and in the footnotes. If we abide by what you ordered, that reports should be complete and understandable, they cannot be complete and understandable unless we have an opportunity to cross-examine this witness thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I present another argument?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I present another argument before you rule on this issue? May I present another argument before you rule?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm convinced that your knowledge and your conclusions about the municipality of Kotor Varos would be quite different had I not cross-examined this witness about this topic. And all the topics where we will not have proper cross-examination should not be a basis for any of your findings, because Kotor Varos was presented here as the case where there were the worst violations, and we have now seen that this is not the case. These are the pillars on which the indictment rests. Donia, Treanor, Hanson, and some other employees of the Prosecution are presented here as impartial experts, and they are the pillars of the indictment. How can we learn what really was going on unless we have an opportunity to cross-examine them thoroughly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. You'll have until the end of today's session. That will be about eight hours and a half. Try your best to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document. This is a session, dated on the 16th of June, 1992, again in Petrovac. And let me just give you a summary. The president reported the situation on the front-line; one person killed, nineteen wounded. And it says here they expect from the Crisis Staff to present a clear position towards the Muslims, and the military post wants that measures be taken against them that would make it impossible for them to operate and to organise in the rear of our forces. And mention is made of about some 40 groups of armed extremists. Thirteen are beyond the reach of police organs, they have fled, and the demand is made to isolate them in order to prevent them from becoming a risk to our forces in the rear. Now, this is a summary, again. Did you take into account these developments as a factor, where some 40 Muslim extremists are located in the rear of our forces and are setting up a military organisation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that there was some armed resistance in some municipalities. Certainly, I read this, I was aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then further down -- - can we have the next page in English? - a decision is made that all persons who possessed weapons illegally or have been registered as Muslim extremists, which renders them a potential danger, shall be detained. And then it goes on to say where the detention facility is going to be located. The explanation: "The steps envisaged by this decision are being implemented against all persons that have armed themselves illegally and organised paramilitary formations with the goal of organising an armed rebellion against the legal authorities because of the general safety of property and citizens. "An additional reason for such action lies in the fact that tensions and anxiety have grown among citizens in the territory of the municipality. And due to the animosity toward the persons cited in paragraph 1 of this decision, endangering their personal safety, which the Crisis Staff has considered in making this decision." So in the depth of the Serb territory, there are groups that pose a danger because they're opening fire on the troops from behind, and the Crisis Staff issues a decision to detain such persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, sorry to interrupt, but can Mr. Karadzic please cite the evidence as it is. The document states "a group of about 40 persons," not "40 groups," which is what he said originally and then proceeded to say, again, "groups."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the problem is in the translation. But I am really rushing, so I would like you to read the document. Ms. Hanson reads Serbian, and everybody else can read the translation. That's why I'm rushing through those documents, because you can all read the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you agree with me, Ms. Hanson, that there was not peace, law and order, in the depth of the Serb territory at this time, but people were being killed, there were attacks, and so on?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this document indicates that there were still some shooting, some fighting.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1340, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have 65 ter 1099.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't want to waste time reading this document. Do you agree with me, Ms. Hanson, that this document is a document in which the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Bosanski Petrovac is asking for additional police, because it says in the second paragraph: "During police curfews, a still unidentified group has been shooting, demolishing and looting taverns, shops and kiosks owned by citizens of Muslim nationality, but since recently also (those owned by citizens) of Serbian nationality, keeping the entire civilian population in anxiety and fear"? And the third and the fourth paragraph of this document says that: "The members of our police have not managed to put a stop to this practice. We assume this is because of the lack of training or because they don't want to -- for somebody to bear a grudge against them, and we would like you to send a unit of the special police in order to prevent the decreasing morale among part of our population ..." And so on and so forth. Are you aware that the authorities are asking for additional special forces to come in to maintain peace and to keep the Muslim community safe?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way they phrase it, not only Muslims, but also recently Serbs are asking for protection. But, yes, they're asking for additional police forces to keep -- to introduce law and order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1341, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have 65 ter 1107.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session of the 7th of July, 1992. I would like us to look at the first paragraph in item 1: "Obrad Vrzina reported on the security situation in the territory of the municipality and assessed it is delicate, with a popular feeling of discontent, especially directed towards the Muslims after the recent events on the front-line, and stressed that the best and a sure solution for the protection of the Muslims would be to move the population. He emphasised that the territory of the municipalities was large, did not easily lend itself to safe-guarding and control, and that the forces were not adequate to the needs." Do you remember that I presented this argument, that I did say that this was a large municipality and that it could not be put under control?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that in the context of a different document, and I said that the answer in that document was not that the municipality was large. Here, I see that. However, as I said before, I recall that most of the Muslims in the municipality were, in fact, found in the town of Petrovac, and their -- the solution they're looking for seems to be to move the Muslims, rather than ensure their -- take extraordinary efforts to ensure their safety here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, do you see here that he says that the municipality is large? And you want to say that there are no Muslims living in the village of Bjelaj, in this municipality. Are you trying to tell me that there were no Muslim villages in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mention the village of Bjelaj because I've never heard of it. I'm not saying there were no Muslim villages. I said the majority were found in the town. But there is no place in Bosnia that is completely one nationality or another, so I'm certain that there were some Muslims beyond the town of Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you see that a statement is made here that in addition to the fact that it is difficult to put this municipality under the control, because it's so large, that there were no adequate forces to meet the needs? And we could see that -- from the previous document that additional police forces were sought. Were the authorities here able to do more, apart from proposing that the population at risk be evacuated, be moved out, because the authorities could not protect them due to lack of appropriate forces?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there could have been other measures, but it's hard to speculate at this point with the information given here. But the members of the -- the commanders of the police, of the local units, were part of the Crisis Staff or, in this case -- yes, still the Crisis Staff. There were armed -- they were in contact with the higher units of the army and so on. I don't know -- it's hard to tell what else could have been done. They certainly decry the lack of law and order. I simply note that their solution to the problem is to move out the population.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1342, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have 65 ter 1114.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is -- this was a session -- or, rather, a decision was made on the 31st of July, 1992, and it says here that the Muslims can move out, on a voluntary basis, provided they sign a contract on the exchange of immovable property and if they sign a statement ceding their property to the state. And then further on, it says that: "Apartments used by Muslims who are holders of occupancy or tenancy rights may only be handed over to the enterprises who own the apartments and the enterprises shall give them for temporary use to their employees, giving priority to --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they can only sell their movable property or give it away by signing a statement to the Municipal Assembly: "Persons who receive movable property are obliged to keep it and cannot transfer it to themselves until the end of the war." And: "All contracts on the exchange of property shall be revised." Did you take into account this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe I cite it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that I revoked and invalidated -- I cancelled all the decisions whereby property was gifted to either the state or a municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1343, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have 65 ter 1115.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date is the 3rd of August, 1992. And on item 2 of the agenda, we can see we have the consideration of the security situation, the issue of Muslims. And then item 2, the second paragraph, it says: "In the course of the session, a group of citizens of Muslim nationality appeared, and they stated they want to attend the session of this commission and to ask some questions. The president and other members of the commission allowed them to put forward their requests or questions.
