"Mase Druzic, Husein Odobasic, Remzo Terzic and Ismet Druzic and Gutlic presented their view of the situation and asked the following questions: "1. Will the workers of Muslim nationality work in companies?" And the second question: "Will the Muslims in Petrovac have their safety guaranteed?" You've read this document. The document is from early August. You cited it as if there had been no development of events; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cite it, yes, in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account the development of events? It's five months into the war.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not discuss the events of the war in any detail in my report, no, but I was aware of them as I wrote the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 100, you say: [In English] "When a delegation of Muslims enquired of the War Commission in Bosanski Petrovac, whether the Muslims would have a guarantee of safety in the municipality, the War Commission responded by forming a commission for the departure of Muslims." [Interpretation] And you treat that as ethnic cleansing, as the intention of Serbian authorities to cleanse Muslims from Petrovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't use the word "ethnic cleansing," or even "cleansing," but I say that their solution to Muslims wanting safety was to move the Muslims out. And that that was one of the things that crisis staffs did, or war commissions in this case, was organise the departure of Muslims, and this is an example of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, if the Serbian authorities had a plan and intention to cleanse or evacuate or expel Muslims from Petrovac, why, then, in the fifth month of the war, was this decision taken that they may evacuate for their own safety? Why were they not driven out immediately?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said repeatedly, Petrovac was a Bosnian Serb majority, and, in general, the Serb authorities may have felt they could control the power sufficiently. The Muslims were concentrated in one spot. As we saw early on, the Muslims were co-operating. The SDA was apparently helping carry out the orders for disarming the Muslim population. They seemed willing to co-operate. Petrovac was one of the groups that said that Muslims should be removed to a level at which Serbian power can be held efficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking now about Sanski Most. We'll come to that if we have time. We're now talking about Petrovac. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Petrovac was one of the municipalities. That document was written in Sanski Most. But representatives of seven municipalities, including Bosanski Petrovac, are named in that document, so I include it as one of the relevant municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1344, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, Ms. Hanson, that the reason for that is the inability to establish control and to provide safety and security?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that given here as the reason, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 65 ter 1138, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The session of 9 September 1992. Paragraph 3: "Pursuant to a decision by the War Presidency and the Resettlement Commission, all citizens of Petrovac wishing to move out of Petrovac municipality will be provided with transport and escort to places to which they wish to move, every day starting with 9 September." Did you review this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that this commission was made up of two Serbs and two Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was that commission that we saw in an earlier document you provided, but the Commission for the Resettlement, I believe, is the one founded in August, in response to the document we had just seen from the 3rd of August. I believe that's when they formed the commission with that name. So it's not clear. It would take a long time to go through all the documents to see just their names, whether they're referring to the earlier one we saw that was half Muslim and half Serb or the one from August.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1345, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1162, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a decision invoking Article 3 on the decision invoking the War Presidency. At the level of the municipality, a service will be formed to take charge of exchanges of flats owned by Muslims and refugees from other areas: "The following shall be appointed to the commission: An officer for housing matters of the Petrovac municipality administration organ; one worker, member of the self-managing community of interest for housing; and one member as a professional person/civilian representative. The commission will draw up a contract which the interested parties will sign and certify." Do you see that this commission is being established as a service to those who want to exchange property?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we've seen property exchanged. The decision already from the summer said that people who wanted to leave would either exchange their property or donate it, so I thought the Commission for Exchanges was already formed. But, yes, here we see them -- the War Presidency setting up a commission for the exchange of property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This says "service." Municipal services are created to cater to those who need a notary public or something like that. The authorities are establishing this service, and this is 8 October -- 28 October. Muslims still lived there, and they want to move out, to move somewhere else. And in order for them not to lose their property, a service is created for them, and for Serbs who had fled from somewhere else, to help them exchange property. Right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does Mr. Karadzic have a question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it right that the municipality is creating a service; not a commission to drive out anyone, but a service to help those who want to swap property?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says both "service" and "commission." The first sentence says "sluzbe," the second session "commission." But, yes, that's what it says. It's being formed for the exchange of property.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this concerns Muslim owners and refugees from other areas? Do you agree that these refugees from other areas refers to Serbs who came to Petrovac, or could it be any refugee?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They simply say "refugee."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 1164. That's the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is also 28 October, end October, and the Presidency takes a decision: "Muslim citizens must enjoy all rights ..." Et cetera, et cetera. And the Public Security Station in Petrovac is instructed to increase patrols in areas where large numbers of Muslims live, and especially in the Bjelaj Local Commune, and also that rigorous measures be proposed against any persons who threaten the Muslims' rights to peace, life and work, and that they be arrested and handed over to judicial authorities. Do you agree that these Muslims are living outside Petrovac, especially concentrated in Bjelaj, and patrols are ordered to pay more attention to these Muslim-inhabited areas?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document would suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you include this document in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1347, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your paragraph 97, you said: [In English] "The status, and exodus of non-Serbs in the Serb municipalities was a constant theme of the Crisis Staff work. The Kljuc Crisis Staff stated that it had resolved issues about the organised emigration of Muslims as well as the very question of the status of Muslims." [Interpretation] Then you say that the War Presidency in Celinac gave a special status to Muslims. Do you know that in Basta, a village in Celinac municipality, five Muslims were killed, and I ordered an investigation? There were these measures in Celinac that Muslims should not walk around during the night so as not to be killed?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know about the killings in Basta, nor your order for an investigation. I don't see anything in that Celinac order that it was for their own safety. It was simply giving them a special status.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that if we have enough time. Paragraph 98. [In English] "In Kljuc, for example, the War Presidency which claimed to have resolved personal issues in the courts, municipal administration, public and state enterprises, set out the criteria for loyalty by which people in mixed marriages could be employed in state or public companies." [Interpretation] Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what my report says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 65 ter 11263 now, please. 11263, for us to see what they were doing in Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This says that on 21st July, the second half of July, Asim Egrlic, until now the president of the Executive Board of Kljuc municipality, is released from his duties of president effective from the 1st of June, 1992. And this was a decision taken on the 21st July only. It was not in the form of a question, but I want the interpreters to add my question always. Is that the example which you used to show how the authorities in Kljuc resolved the issue of employment in various organs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one such example, but it's not the one I cite to that sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll come to those you used as well. May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1348, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 65 ter 11264.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this another example that Omer Filipovic, until that moment vice-president of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc, is also discharged from his duties?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this as another such example.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we admit this? And we will remember the names E grlic and Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1349, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 822, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this material is handwritten at the Public Security Station, Kljuc. It says, "just before the ethnic cleansing of Kljuc," et cetera, et cetera. Now I ask for the next page. This was written by someone who found this document. The note on the first page is by someone who collected this document; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it appears, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see what those Muslims we had referred to were doing. "The Crisis Staff ..." [In English] "... which operated before, but was dissolved immediately before the armed conflicts." [Interpretation] Muhamed Filipovic, SDA party and member of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly; Omer Filipovic, commissioner; Asim Egrlic, political figure. We see all these names of people who were members of that Crisis Staff in the municipality. All these people were employed with the municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these people? The names you've listed, yes, were apparently employed with the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these the two who had been dismissed from the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We see, therefore, that they also owned independent companies for protection, independent platoons or a platoon. Can we see the next page. The next page speaks about the military organisation of Muslims in Kljuc. In Velagici there's one company, a commander, one platoon, and so on. The structure of that unit in Krasulje, the same. The commander is Muratagic. There is a reference to prison. Can we see the next page? Did you see this document? Did you review this document that refers to the military organisation in all local communes and villages inhabited by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw these notes. My understanding is they are notes by the Kljuc Serbian police. They are what they've learned about the Muslim organisation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted? I cannot go on through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1350, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 18817. 11 -- sorry, 18817.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we see the Crisis Staff of Kljuc informs - it's probably a press release or something - informs that all citizens of Velecevo and Dubocani who had surrendered weapons, illegally-purchased weapons, are given guarantee of security. And it says the Crisis Staff holds the position that all regular units of the Serbian Army should not take any forcible measures or actions against these citizens, with a view to maintaining the existing security situation and protecting the citizens. If any of the parties fail to honour this proclamation, the offenders will be subject to all the measures envisaged in these cases. Did you review this?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably saw it, although I'm not immediately familiar with it. It's not an unusual document to me. So I can't say that I -- I can't say 100 per cent that I reviewed it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted, MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1351, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Pending translation, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 65 ter 905.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree this is a report on the work and activities of the Kljuc Public Security Station, that is, the police station, during combat operations on the territory of Kljuc municipality? It's July 1992, covering these three months of war. I said "July." Didn't I say "July"?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 3 in Serbian and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The status of the municipality, Krajina -- and then towards the middle, it says: "In view of the fact it was clear that the concept of unitarian BH cannot succeed, all the activities of SDA were aimed at creating a Muslim municipality, which was, in fact, done in December, 1992, with the proclamation of the Bosnian Municipality of Kljuc." That's towards the top in English. We need the previous page in English.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not seeing it in B/C/S or English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3 in English and in Serbian, item 4. Those are second pages in both versions. We need the third page. It's different in e-court, I suppose. We need the Serbian as well. Here, item 4, towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Muslims had established their own municipality of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that there was a division/separation in the municipality. It's the only one where I see Muslim -- or an equivalent action on the Muslim side, equivalent to the Serb declarations of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is more: Prijedor, Sanski Most, Vlasenica, Bratunac, Madam. Well, we can remain on this page in English. Everything was arranged, and had they not reneged on it, the Muslims in those municipalities, there would not have been a war. But you knew that there were so many municipalities where talks were in progress, and in some of those municipalities, the appropriate agreements had already been reached. Kljuc was not the only one. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not see any agreement on the division of municipalities before the declaration of Serbian municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please pay attention to Chapter 3: "The basic objective and task of the Public Security Station was to monitor all events of interest for the security and finding solutions, lest there should be a war. The objectives were implemented relatively successfully up until the end of May 1992." And then further on it says: "Our municipality was one of the rare -- one of the few municipalities where we did not have any open inter-ethnic conflicts." Do you know that they managed to maintain peace until the end of May in the municipality of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would also just note an error in the English translation. It says "the first quarter of 1991." It should be "1992." It doesn't make sense there, "1991."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at page 6 in the Serbian version, which would be page 4 in the English language. So it's the next page in English and one page further down in Serbian. I think we need to go one page further in English, too. We need Roman numeral IV.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, here we see "Goals of the Armed Rebellion" on the part of the Muslim side. It says: "It has been two months since the Muslim extremists and fundamentalists started their armed rebellion in the area of Kljuc municipality." And can we now move on to the next page, both in Serbian and in English, item 5, where it says -- well, I have to summarise because I don't have enough time to read through. And I would like Ms. Hanson to look at this paragraph, if that was the gist of your objection. Please look at item 5, "Operative Intelligence," which has shown that there is a parallel system of the Muslim Territorial Defence under the command of Omer Filipovic, who was the president of the MVO in Kljuc and a member of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly, and he's a reserve lieutenant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is what correct? That's what the text says, if that's what you mean, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the same Omer Filipovic who was fired; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at the next page, and the last paragraph before the next chapter, where it says: "The attacks began on the 27th of May in the entire valley of the Sana River." Do you know that in late May, there was an all-out attack by the Muslims on Serbs and the Serb municipalities in the Sana valley, Sanski Most, Prijedor, Bosanski Novi and Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: An all-out attack? No, I am not aware of an all-out attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at item 6. It speaks about the armed activities in the area of the Kljuc municipality, and it says that it started on the 27th of May, 1992. On that day, the Muslim extremists and fundamentalists carried out a synchronised set of armed actions against members of the police and the military of the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina. Were you not aware of that, were you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you were speaking so fast. Where is the reference? Item 6, yes. I've seen this report, so I have seen this description of this ambush. However, the tone of the report and its sources are such that I take it with a grain of salt. One ambush is not an all-out co-ordinated attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will list them in a minute, Ms. Hanson. And I'm asking you: Are you an expert, and was it your task to determine which documents to include and which to exclude, which documents were valid and which were not, or is it something that is incumbent upon the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my job, as an expert, to make a selection of documents to include in my report, and part of my selection is based on their credibility and their relationship between the language they use and the reality of events. I looked at this, but I also looked at the report on the work of the Crisis Staff. And since my report was based on the work of crisis staffs, I relied on that report. But I certainly read this one, and I read those police notes. It's wonderful that the Trial Chamber has a chance to read them all, but a selection is part of my job as an -- in writing an expert report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now see what kind of a job you did. Can we please look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On that day, hour by hour, we can see how many synchronised armed operations were launched against the police, the military, and the citizens. That's Serbian page 9. That would be page 9 in the Serbian version, item 1, "Ambush in the area of Gornji Ramici, and it's the same page in the English language. That's page 6 -- that's page 6 in the English version. Yes, I can see that we have the right page: "Setting up an ambush in the Gornji Ramici Sector around 9:00 a.m." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move on to the next page both in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 2, "Ambush in the area of Busija and the village of Perin Han." At 1400 to 1430 hours, this operation was organised and commanded by Amir Avdic and Nezir Djedic [phoen], and about 80 extremists took part in it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the text says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 3, "Ambush in the area of Tocina." Item 4, "Blowing up the M5 road between the area of Velagici and Laniste." Do you see this was done on the same day?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the previous page, it says that -- well, we don't have enough time to go back, but Omer Filipovic is again mentioned. Can we move on to the next page? We can remain on the same page in English. Item 5, "Attack on the check-point in Velagici." Item 6, "Capture of seven Serbian BH Army soldiers in the Crljeni Village Sector." Item 7, "Use of our Forces." So the six combat actions on the same day, targeting the Serb army, police and Serbs, themselves, in the depth of the Serb territory, is that tantamount to armed rebellion or not?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know -- when you say "in the depth," I don't know the exact location of these places in the municipality. When you say "Serb territory," if there are Muslims there, it is not completely Serb territory. As for armed rebellion, that's a question beyond the scope of my report or expertise on what counts as a rebellion and what is a -- you know, what is the status of the Serb government against which these inhabitants appear to be rising.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, you based your reports on documents. That's what you told us yesterday. You said that you did not take into account any witness testimony and so on. Were you in the municipality of Kljuc in late May 1992 or did you base your report on documents?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Kljuc in late May 1992. I based my report on documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So at page 63 of the transcript, line 5, you say that you compared documents with the situation in the field. Did you check whether this was the situation in the field in the municipality of Kljuc in late May, and did you make a comparison, and then, based on your comparison, you decided not to use this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I decided not to use this document because it deals mostly with police matters, and I am dealing with crisis staffs, so I used the report on the work of crisis staffs. I also found this quite tendentious in its references to fundamentalists and that kind of terminology. I don't deny -- I have no basis to accept or deny their accounts of these specific attacks. It's when they discuss the political objectives of people who had been elected to municipal government positions and describe them as fundamentalists and extremists, that's where I felt this report, itself, was straining its own credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, you are saying that the municipal authorities, the crisis staffs and so on, were arresting people, detaining people. How can they arrest them or detain them, if not with the use of police? Do you know that after this rebellion, this instance of rebellion, 1.280 citizens, or, rather, rebels, armed rebels who took part in the armed rebellion, were, in fact, arrested in this area? It was after the rebellion, not before?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the page reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the page number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12 in Serbian, 004 and so on, and it's page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder if you can answer now, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm aware there were arrests at this time. I don't know the figure, and I don't know if it was specifically of people who were known to have taken part in armed action. I'm not going to accept the use of the word "rebellion" here; that seems a bit tendentious. But, yes, here it says that 1.278 citizens were sent to prisoner-of-war camps, and it lists the criterion by which they were sent to the camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were they arrested because of their religion or ethnicity or because of what they did, and the things they did are listed here?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their list -- the criterion on which they were arrested is listed. Some of them are a bit vague, and there's no indication that Serbs who owned weapons without a permit were arrested. There's no indication that Serbs who took an active part in spreading propaganda in order to provoke ethnic hatred were arrested. I believe the people who were arrested and sent to camps were non-Serbs, but this criterion does not say they were arrested purely on the basis of their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say that they were arrested, inter alia, on the basis of their ethnicity, or is it that it is their contact that was the reason why they were arrested, or was it, inter alia, they were Muslims? You are excessively partial, Madam. The conduct is the reason for their arrest. Were all Muslims in Kljuc arrested or only those who took part in those actions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all Muslims were arrested, but not all persons who owned weapons without a permit were arrested. Not all persons who took an active part in provoking ethnic hatred were --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's your speculation, Madam, that's your speculation. You don't have evidence for that. This document does not contain proof of that. It says that there were 12.000 Muslims and only 1.200 and odd were arrested. And we saw the list of those who were in those units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document doesn't say 1200 Muslims, as far as I read it. It says "persons." Right down at the very bottom, the very last one, it says "persons who belong to the so-called Muslim TO or persons who actively took part in the organisation and formation of the so-called Muslim TO." That's the only reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you dismissed this document. It was your assessment that it did not merit your attention; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not included in my report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1352, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to look at paragraph 99 of your report: [In English] "The Crisis Staffs carried out the policies and procedures of the forcible departure of non-Serbs. In Bosanska Krupa, the War Presidency, in its own words, "suggested two options to the Muslims: either to organise their own evacuation from the area or to have that effected by military means." [Interpretation] Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you took one document out of the context and you characterise it in this way, and you formed your position on the basis of that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have many more than one document cited in the footnote of the first sentence of that paragraph. The citation footnote 170, is only to that one quotation, although I notice -- note other relevant documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph -- or, rather, in footnote 177, you use, as an example of forced evacuation of the population, you use document 65 ter 6707. Can we have 65 ter 6707. You do know the place that is mentioned here, Arapusa; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Arapus a personally. I'm familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say in your footnote -- you mention it in your footnote 177; right? You give this as an example of a crime committed by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not give it as an example of a crime committed by Serbs. I give it as an example of a crisis staff organising the removal of the population of a Muslim village. I do not describe it as a crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, do you see that document in the footnote referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he meant 170, not 177. No, that's Podgrmec, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Arapusa is mentioned specifically in footnote 177, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see it, so could you check?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it's the bottom of page -- the bottom of the page that has paragraph 101 on it, under "Bosanska Krupa," under footnote 177, the second item.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at this document, Ms. Hanson. This document speaks about the evacuation in a column where people would be using their own vehicles. The column would be secured by the battalion. And upon their departure from the border post where the battalion command was, "the battalion command on the Bozo Erceg will be responsible for providing security for the entire village of Arapusa and all movable and immovable property." Can we move on to page 2? We can remain on page 1 in the English version and move to page 2 in the Serbian version. "On the basis of an agreement with the War Staff Command of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanska Krupa, Mr. Miroslav Vjestica, as soon as peace is established, the command is obliged to ensure the safe return of the residents to their homes in Arapusa and the refugees to Bosanska Krupa." The refugees from Bosanska Krupa to Bosanska Krupa. Do you see that this was signed on behalf of the Executive Committee of the Arapusa Local Commune, Emir Sejdic, a Muslim; and for the Committee of the refugees from Bosanska Krupa, a man by the name of Fuad Djugomovic, Fuad, again a Muslim; and on behalf of the battalion command, it was Bozo Erceg and Djordjo Jez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the document indicates, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you use this as an example of the expulsions of the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the 65 ter number of this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6707, I believe, 6707.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is 17272?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that's the previous one. Has it been admitted? No, the previous one was 905.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I refer to the number which is cited in a footnote.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's where I found it. Sometimes documents have duplicates and there might be more than one 65 ter number, but I don't know if that's true in this case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the same document under a different number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, we admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1353, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to look at 65 ter 6703.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see this, that the date is the 19th of April, 1993? It's a report by the Executive Board, so that's regular authorities. They have submitted their report about the spontaneous migration of the population. The Serbs crossed the River Una, from the left bank to the right bank, and the Muslims moved in the opposite direction. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see no reference here to spontaneous migration, just an exchange of population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it says here at the outbreak of war, there was a migration of the population. Serbs from the left bank of the Una crossed to the right. So they were not moved. They left, themselves.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this Serb -- member of the Serbian municipal government, yes, that's the term he uses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you agree with me that we have Bosanska Krupa and Srpska Krupa, two municipalities that are divided by the river? --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had the Serbs declare the Serbian Municipality of Krupa, so by default, the other municipality or the municipality that was not part of the Serbian municipality remained Bosanska Krupa, but it was not an agreed division, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that talks were under way, and they would have been successful had not the SDA central [as interpreted] intervened and prevented this?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no basis for knowing that the talks would have been successful, nor that the SDA intervened.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1354, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your last question before the break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to look at 65 ter 6711.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is an overview of persons arrested, or captured and arrested, on the 21st and 22nd of April, 1992, in an armed conflict in Bosanska Krupa. And we have a list of 12 people who were captured. And the third person on the list, Sadrija Djudja, was transferred to the refugees because an assessment was probably made that he had not taken part in the fighting. Did you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've seen it, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1355, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Ms. Hanson, we cannot dwell on Krupa any longer, or some other municipalities. But Krupa, as you confirmed, is the place where the president of the Crisis Staff, Mr. Klickovic, was acquitted before the Bosnian Court. I'd like to come back to the instructions, what the central organs were doing. In your paragraph 38, you said: [In English] "On 26 April, 1992, the Government of the Republika Srpska issued instructions for the work of crisis staffs of the Serbian people in municipalities." [Interpretation] Then in paragraph 43, you said that crisis staffs acted in accordance with these instructions for crisis staffs. Is that correct? Is it right that you say that they received and applied the instructions of the government?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. D407, please, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is D407. Is this an excerpt from the instructions for the work of crisis staffs, signed by Prime Minister Djeric on the 26th of April? We'll see that on the next page. That's the report that is meant; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the versions. The version I used is in Cyrillic. But it's one of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in Article 1, it says: "The Crisis Staff, under circumstances of war, takes over all the prerogatives and the functions of municipal assemblies, when these are unable to convene." And item 3 says: "The Crisis Staff co-ordinates functions of the authorities for the purposes of defending territory ..." It co-ordinates functions of the existing authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "co-ordinates the functions of authority." The translation said "existing authority." I don't see that exact word in there. I don't know if it's a question of the translation or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you understand that it's not a new government? The Crisis Staff is made up of the members of the existing authorities, ex officio?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says it's the work of crisis staffs of the Serbian people in municipalities. I don't see that the -- it's not specified that they be all Serbs, the way it was in the 19 December instructions. But the crisis staffs I see that operate according to this don't -- don't include the non-Serb office-holders. These are the organs of the Serbian people, the Serbian municipalities or municipal assemblies. So it's not purely ex officio, in that if the elected president of the Municipal Assembly was a Muslim, I don't see him included on the crisis staffs that operate, according to these instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we decided to have our own municipalities, how would a Muslim be elected a representative of the Serbian people in that municipality, and how did you determine that Djeric is referring to the 19th December paper? Where is it written that he had ever known about that paper?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He makes no reference in this to the 19 December instructions. I see the continuity described in the documents of the organs, themselves, that describe the continuity between the organs formed upon the 19 December instructions and the municipal organs here. But you asked about the "ex officio" question. I'm saying that these are only from the offices of the declared Serbian municipal assemblies. I think we agree on the "ex officio" question. As for indications that Djeric had ever heard of the 19 December instructions, I'd have to check whether he was at those Assembly sessions at which they were discussed, but they were certainly discussed in the Assembly. And as we saw, declarations of municipal assemblies taken on the basis of the 19 December instructions were published in "Javnost," so we certainly couldn't exclude that he heard of them. They were also published in "Oslobodjenje," just about the -- no, it was in late March 1992, so he would have heard of them, most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Madam, please, do you have any document by Djeric where he says that he is acting upon the basis of the 19th December 1991 document; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting: Ms. Hanson, do you allow the possibility that the paper of the 19th December and this paper, too, have some common ground, and that the 19th December paper is not the ground paper, the fundamental paper? There is another basic document for all of this. It's called the Law on All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly agree that the paper of 19 December and this paper have some common ground; it's the crisis staffs of the Serbian people. As for the Law on All People's Defence, they do call for the creation of the council. All People's Defence committees, as I indicated in my report, I see some common ground, some commonality, between those organs and the crisis staffs. However, neither this document by Djeric, nor the 19 December instructions, explicitly refer to the committees for all people's defence, all people's defence, or to the Law on All People's Defence. As far as I know, the Law on All People's Defence does not use the term "crisis staffs," so I can't see a direct connection, but I do see, in the documents of the crisis staffs and war presidencies, themselves, that they see a direct chain from the 19 December instructions of party crisis staffs to Djeric's instructions on municipal crisis staffs, and I see a continuity between those bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Karadzic. Can we see -- just for the purpose of a reminder, can we see the 19th of December document? Do you have that exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: P960, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you up-load it briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can leaf through to see where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because there was several versions, I now know what it was. Please proceed. Let's go back to D407.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see in this document items 9 and 10, what Prime Minister Djeric instructs the crisis staffs to do? Items 9, 10 and 13. I don't want to read. Let everyone read it themselves. You said this was applied. You said the instructions of the government were applied. Was this applied?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work with international peace-making and humanitarian organisations, we certainly see -- have seen that discussion of the International Red Cross. The unhindered transport of humanitarian aid was not always observed. Article 10 again cites the International Red Cross and acting humanely towards -- or utterly humanely towards the combats -- non-combatants and humanely towards war prisoners. Again, we see crisis staffs involved in these issues, including the condition of prisoners, including talking to the International Red Cross. So to that extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The basic question in paragraph 43 is that they received it and acted upon it. Do you stand by that, that they received the instructions and acted upon them?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see D408.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One day later, Prime Minister Djeric -- or, rather, the Ministry for Health-Care and Social Protection sends instructions to all regional staffs to act humanely with humanitarian convoys, to enable treatment of the wounded and the ill, regardless of nationality and faith, that international norms have to be observed in the treatment of prisoners of war. Did you take into account this, this instruction from a ministry to crisis staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I did. But had I seen it, I would certainly have included it because -- as I have bemoaned the lack of documentation on regional crisis staffs. So if something from the Ministry of Health -- if you'll allow me to check my notes, I'll see if I've included this one or not. But I would have, had I seen it. It certainly supports my conclusion that the regional crisis staffs were also operating in the state system. I'm sorry, I can't find it right now, but I would have included it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Ms. Hanson, these are instructions from the central level of government to crisis staffs. Do you agree that everything coming from central authorities indicates that they want to preserve law and order? Did you find any document from the central level that would be contrary to this?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- as I say, I didn't see this one, that I recall. I would certainly have included it. It certainly is expecting correct conduct, in accordance with international law, so it's very much in that. As for the broader question of anything coming, some of them -- I don't -- no, they generally -- where they refer to international -- or to law and order, they are for the maintenance of law and order, I'm struggling a little because I'm trying to recall every document I've seen, but I do not see them urging any illegal activities, if that's what you're trying -- the -- when they refer to law and order, yes, they are trying to preserve law and order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the record, this document, because we didn't see the signature, was signed by then Minister of Health Dragan Kalinic, who was a member of the government from an opposition party. Could we now see P1095.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you help us, Ms. Hanson, whether the original was written in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It certainly appears to be the original in English. That's the one with the stamp and the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1095, please. These are minutes from the 28th session of the government, dated 15 June. The last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The second paragraph: "The session --" The last page but one in English: "The session indicated the high importance of ensuring the functioning of government and overall life in all parts of the republic; inter alia, republic commissioners should contribute to that because they are representatives of all republic organs." Do you see that already in early June, after the decision to abolish crisis staffs was taken, the government is trying to help out local authorities by sending commissioners?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is just five days after the presidential decision on the formation of war commissions. I would just note, for the Court's assistance, that here in the translation, the word "povjerenik" has been translated as "trustee," but that's the word that is usually translated as "commissioner," so it is a reference to war commissioners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's an issue in our language. We don't like the word "commissioner" because it reminds us of "komesar," so perhaps "trustee" is not bad.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D440. Let us see how the vice-president of the republic, Koljevic, on 16 July 1992, expressed his dissatisfaction with his own control and influence over these commissioners. The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He says that he is dissatisfied, he's offering his resignation, and he says it's not about the work of the Presidency, but its contribution. He stressed he cannot govern republic commissioners, which he considers to be his failure. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and then Momcilo Krajisnik was replaced as the member of the Presidency responsible for commissioners. But in this session, Koljevic is trying to resign altogether from the Presidency. He says the whole work is too much for him and he's dissatisfied with his performance. And the other members want him to stay on, and he does, but some jobs are taken away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He says he cannot govern republican commissioners; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what Koljevic says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's look at D445.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it look to you, Ms. Hanson, like the authorities are bending over backwards to try to change the situation on the ground? They are changing crisis staffs and war presidencies and creating commissioners?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it looks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at this. This is a proclamation to the citizens of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; citizens, mind you, not Serbs. The second paragraph refers to Geneva Conventions, which stipulate that civilians in war-afflicted areas must be allowed to evacuate. Furthermore, evacuation has to be voluntary. Therefore, it cannot be either obstructed or encouraged. And the second sentence: "The authorities of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina are not forcibly keeping citizens in war zones, because otherwise the citizens would be hostages, nor are they forcibly transferring them because that would be ethnic cleansing. All refugees from the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina will be allowed to return without suffering any consequences. Only criminals, not civilians, are subject to legal sanctions." Were you aware of this proclamation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you include it in your report as a reference to the activity and work of the central organs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because my focus was, as I said before, on municipal crisis staffs, and this doesn't directly address crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 65 ter -- could it be P1112? 65 ter 11273 -- 65 ter 11273. This is a session of the Cabinet on the 14th September 1992 in Bijeljina. We see that on page 1. Can we see the next page in Serbian. This is obviously my handwriting and my diary. Let us then see page 6 in English. I cannot even understand my handwriting. We need page 6 in English. Let's see what Prime Minister Djeric says: [In English] "War is chaos, but it is a fact that each minister must be held responsible, the MUP in particular." [Interpretation] Page 7 in English: "Crisis staffs ..." [In English] " ... are authorised to do whatever pleased them, and now it is difficult to return everything to what it used to be. "Bad working conditions, bad communications"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this was in mid-September 1992, and we were still having problems restoring normal functioning, and in some places crisis staffs still exist?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the original? It certainly sounds it. But by September, I don't see many crisis staffs. Many municipal assemblies were already -- had already met in July or August/September. "Crisis staffs were authorised to do whatever pleased them" I see as part of giving them the initiative, but with the -- initiative to take action on the ground, giving them considerable latitude, but they were still seen as part of the system. "And now it's difficult to return everything to how it used to be." I don't know if he's referring to pre-war or before the formation of crisis staffs. That's not -- that's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you said yourself that the crisis staffs were activated in early April, when the war broke out. But the point here is the prime minister is actually saying that it is difficult to achieve that everyone can return because there is a chaos, and the crisis staffs were doing whatever they wanted. It's difficult to go back to the way things were before. And he is talking about bad communications and bad conditions of work. Do you agree with me that this is the position of the government in early September?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe Djeric even tried to resign over -- at about this time. I'm not exactly sure of the chronology, but he complained, similarly, that he is having trouble working because -- his working conditions were poor because he was left out of -- he wasn't receiving a lot of information. He tried to resign, I believe. But, again, I did not review the chronology of the republican level at this time for my report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless it has already been admitted. I'm not sure. It hasn't been admitted yet, so can it then be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1356, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have 1D3590. We don't have enough time to present everything that we have on Prijedor. Let us look at a report, how things were in Prijedor until the end of 1992. So this is a report. We're still waiting for the English version. This is a report for the period between the 11th of September until the 26th of December, 1992, in Prijedor municipality. It's a party report filed by the Municipal Board of the SDS. Now I would like us to go to page 7 in Serbian and page 6 in English. Page 6 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like you to turn your attention to the penultimate passage here: "When the war broke out, on the orders of the leadership at Pale, the crisis staffs are formed, later on war presidencies, to replace the municipal boards, and the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS and the People's deputy were not members thereof." And then it goes on to say that: "During the time of war and the secession of party activities, there were no contacts with the central office of the party or the state leadership of the Serbian Republic," or Republika Srpska. And the last passage here says: "Communication was not established until September 1992." Are you aware of the fact that the central organs were not able to communicate with the western part of Bosnia throughout this time? And here we see the example of Prijedor to corroborate that.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see this contradicted, for example, by the Prijedor decision on the work of the crisis staffs, which, as we noted, in some places is a literal transcription of Djeric's instructions. So they did receive those guide-lines. I have heard -- I know this issue of communications has come up before, and there were times when communications were difficult, but they were often restored as well. So, in fact, since I've seen evidence, first of all, that the Crisis Staff was formed well before the beginning of the war, so I tend not to believe that statement then, because I know they received Djeric's guide -- I tend not to believe the statement that they received no guide-lines or general directions from the leaders of the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a report of the Serbian Democratic Party and that they say that they have not been in touch with the central organs? I'm not talking about the Executive Board, I'm not talking about the municipality. I'm talking about the party. The party was not represented in the Crisis Staff. It has ceased its operation, and it did not have any contacts with the headquarters -- party headquarters in Pale; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the SDS party was not represented in the Crisis Staff, I don't think that's correct. Yes, I've heard -- I've seen considerable reference throughout Bosnia to the order on the freezing of party activities during the war or, basically, from the outbreak of the war to the beginning of 1993, so I'm familiar with that. But as I note, it's the party leadership in the municipalities who generally become the leaders of the Crisis Staff and now are communicating with the republican level via state organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it says here, quite clearly, in the War Presidency there are no representatives of the SDS, and the people's deputy is not there either, and they did not have any contacts with the central level of the government of Republika Srpska until September 1992. So do you reject this or do you agree with it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the president of the SDS Municipal Board was not on the Crisis Staff or War Presidency. It doesn't say that the SDS had no representation there. And I reject parts of this, because I don't think they're true. As I said, I have evidence to the contrary, so I do not accept this report entirely. And one of the things I do not accept is that they received no guide-lines from the leaders of the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the diary that we looked at a little while ago, if we had time, we would point your attention to where it says that they had not had contact for 45 days with the representatives from Prijedor. But we don't have the time. Can we go to page 8 in the Serbian version. That's page 6 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, it says to this day, strong ties have not been established with the party grassroots and the main board of the party in Pale, although it had been arranged at the last meeting, because the personnel was not brought up to the same level by the SDS, as they were supposed to do. Strong centres of power have been created - that's page 6 in the English version - which are not under party control. This whole passage begins with the words: "Since July ..." Now we're on page 7 in the English version, and we need page 6.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is discussing the party relations, as I make clear in my report. With the shift to public government functions of crisis staffs, the linking -- the linkage went through state organs and the party work was frozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see here that by the end of December, proper communication has not been established yet between the party headquarters and the party bodies in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it notes that a session of the Assembly was held in Prijedor, which certainly indicates some kind of communication and accessibility. But, again, this is about the work of the party board, and I agree that there was a freeze announced on party work at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1357, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you claim, in your paragraph 13, that the party, the SDS, used this undefined term, which is "the crisis staff," ... [In English] "And applied it to a different kind of body, a party organ which claimed the authority of a collective municipal presidency." Do you mean to say that identical party -- that the party crisis staff and municipal party staffs are identical, as state authorities, from April 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note that in some places when they became public municipal authorities, some -- the membership sometimes was expanded. I know in Prijedor, there were more changes than usual, but we do see a crisis staff formed in Prijedor on the 19 December instructions and operating in public in April. Most of the bodies which are public municipal authorities, in late spring/summer of 1992, quite openly trace their origin back to the party organs of 19 December 1991. I agree, in Prijedor there was some personnel change.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the crisis staffs of the party were not able and were not authorised to do anything more than just report to the party headquarters about the events, and that the municipal crisis staffs actually exercised power, and their composition was different, well, is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Authorised" is a difficult question here. We're talking about authorisation of party crisis staffs. On what authority? On the authority of the president of the party, they were told to take over the police stations, for example. And I say there is some differences in composition. The -- some personnel was added when they became municipal crisis staffs, but the continuity is there. They saw themselves as founded on the 19 December instructions. You, yourself, cite the 19 December instructions as the founding document that created secret governments in minority municipalities, and those became the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you're not making any distinction between municipal crisis staffs, as authorities, and the party crisis staffs, as internal party bodies, whose only power was to report and nothing else; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with the entire statement, because I don't say that party -- as internal party organs, their only power was to report, and nothing else. But, essentially, I see a continuity between the two, between party crisis staffs in December 1991 and public crisis staffs in April 1992. But I refuse to comment on -- or I just don't feel I can comment on what were the powers of the party crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, by way of example, I don't have a document here, but you say that the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Democratic Party from Bijeljina is reporting to the Main Board about something that was happening in Bijeljina, and I'm telling you the Crisis Staff of the Bijeljina Serbian Democratic Party is reporting to the party headquarters about what the defence council of Bijeljina is doing, as a state authority. So the party organ is simply reporting to the party headquarters about what state authorities and another state organ is doing; is that so or not?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report of the police from Bijeljina says that under the leadership of the SDS Crisis Staff, Arkan's volunteers and the Serbian TO were operating in the municipality. So although, yes, that document you mentioned is simply a report, other documents indicate that the same Crisis Staff was actually doing other things, including co-ordinating the take-over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Party crisis staff or the municipal crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: SDS Crisis Staff is, I believe, how the police report refers to it, but I'd have to check the exact citation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We don't have the time. Bijeljina will be on the agenda later on. I would like to have this document admitted, and then we can look at 65 ter 3719. It's been admitted? Okay. Can we look at 65 ter 3719.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I will put it to you that everything that was done, including the participation of the ruling party, was done under the Law on All People's Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and the Law on All People's Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember -- well, you noted that the president of the League of Communists of Bosnia-Herzegovina headed the Security Council or the Defence Council. And you said that if we were to replace the League of Communists with the Serbian Democratic Party, it would become quite clear why Karadzic became the head of the Council for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I refer to replacing the League of Communists with the SDS, I'm talking about the municipal borders. I don't -- municipal organisations. I don't believe I mention Karadzic there. It simply says -- paragraph 15 is talking about if you replace SDS for League of Communists, you can see that the municipal crisis -- I don't say "municipal," I'm sorry, that's what I'm referring to, they refer these committees more than they do the municipal presidencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the League of Communists was there because it was the ruling party at the time, and that after the elections in Serb areas, the Serbian Democratic Party came into power, and that this formed the basis for the substitution?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Serb areas" is a problem. In the Serb-majority municipalities, yes, the SDS had the majority of municipal positions, but there was no area that was completely Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this Federal Law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cite in my report the republic law, but I'm familiar with the federal, and I think they're in accordance with each other.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at Article 13. I don't know what page it is, but can you just browse through it until we reach Article 13 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see here that: "Workers and citizens have an obligation and the right to organise themselves and to take part in the organisation/preparation for an implementation of All People's Defence, to educate for All People's Defence, and for the carrying out of tasks in time of war, in the event of an immediate threat of war and other emergencies; to take part in armed struggle and other forms of All People's Defence --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic is kindly asked to read a bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you don't have to read out everything. If you mean to read something, slow down. So now we have Article 13. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see Articles 13, 14 and 15, which stipulate that this is not only a right, but an obligation to take part in the defence of the country, and one of the articles say that there need not be a call-up and that people should take part in defending their country wherever they are at the given moment?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't had time to read everything, but I certainly know that that's the intention of this law. I agree that that's the intention of this law.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at Article 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 17 specifies the rights and obligations in greater detail. Do you agree that this law stipulates that even social and political communities and organs of companies and other communities are duty-bound to ensure that conditions are there in order to enable citizens to meet the obligations from Articles 1 and 2 of this law?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that in the republican law, the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it is stipulated in Article 5 -- well, we'll get it in e-court, but we don't have it here. It says if there is an imminent threat of war or other emergency situation, or if there is an attack on the country, citizens and workers, and social and political communities, and work organisations are duty-bound to carry out their duties in the defence of the country, and act in accordance with their war assignment, and with the appropriate plan, defence plan, without being called up to do so?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall Article 5, that it says that. I would not be surprised that it does. But without the article in front of me, I can't confirm it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to admit this federal law, and then if we can call up the republican law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1351, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have 65 ter 18606. Now please find Article 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you read Serbian. Look at the second paragraph in Article 5, where it says: "Without being called up or without receiving a specific order ..." Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I thought that the entire law would be translated, because this is a 65 ter document, but that doesn't seem to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You used the Serbian version when you studied this law; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I must have. If it hasn't all been translated, I must have.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at Article 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 16, you can see that this is -- it is a duty of workers and citizens to ensure that intelligence is given, and Article 18 specifies that citizens must comply with the work obligation in line with the law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was scrolled by pretty fast. Article 16, could I see it in its entirety? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "To maintain weapons and equipment that they have been issued with, in line with their wartime assignment; to inform the alerting centre, the appropriate organ of the local commune, or other organs, of any events that will affect national security and that they have observed."
