Do you know the indictment charges us that we actually gave the tasks to the organs in the field to monitor the transportation of weapons through their territory and to monitor and report all other events that were relevant for the defence of the country?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that exact part of the indictment, no, but, I mean, I know that that's -- I don't see it -- I don't remember it as a charge in the indictment. I'm familiar with it in the reports on the development of the party, on events in Bosnia. But as a specific charge in the indictment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that under this law, citizens are duty-bound to report any events that are significant for the defence, and everybody in the British Isles would be able to understand that quite well?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the British Isles, I'm sorry, I don't know where that came from. Was that in the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, just disregard that, please. Look at this text.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is expect -- they are expected to be -- expected to do those things to the responsible authorities, which are their municipal- or republic-level authorities. They are supposed to do this within the existing political system.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at Article 18, which regulates work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You knew, did you not, that the workers who were not engaged in the army were subject to work obligation, they had to perform the assignments that were given to them under the work obligation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said I was familiar with that concept of work obligation, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at Article 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that here, in the documents and in the evidence of various experts, there was some criticism levied towards work organisations because they paid their profits into the municipal treasury, or, rather, to the treasury of the Crisis Staff? Do you agree with me that Article 33 obliges companies to secure strategic stockpiles and to carry out other preparations for the defence, in line with their capacities and other capabilities?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see Article 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 1 says: "To organise themselves and prepare for conducting armed struggle, and applying other forms of resistance to the enemy. Organise control and protection of local communes and security for facilities, and for those needs to form Territorial Defence units." All these paragraphs are important. Item 5: "To organise and conduct preparations to mobilise citizens assigned into the armed forces, in keeping with the relevant plan of the municipality." Did you know that the Serbian Democratic Party is accused of encouraging people to respond to mobilisation call-ups into the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- it specifies that it's supposed to be according to the plan of the municipality. As for the charge -- accusation, again, I don't know that it's an accusation in the indictment. It is certainly discussed in the history or in the pre-trial brief, that the SDA -- SDS - I'm sorry, I'm getting tired - the SDS encouraged people to respond to the mobilisation call-ups. But that it's an accusation, I wouldn't frame it as such.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at Article 50. It's on the screen. It says that: "Local communes may enlarge. They can jointly organise institutions and units of territorial defence and civilian protection units."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that written here in this article?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Article 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Socio-political organisations, that means parties, associations, et cetera, correct, also have certain obligations related to national defence, and they direct the activity of their members; correct? Article 52 --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still reading Article 51. So far, it agrees with what you've said, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see Article 52 and 53, referring to the League of Communists and the Socialist Alliance, as the ruling parties at the time, and their obligations regarding defence.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the League of Communists is the carrier of ideo-political activities.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we just scroll down a little to see about the Socialist Alliance of the Working People. Let's see what socio-political communities, such as municipalities and the republic, are supposed to do. Can we see Article 58, "The Association of War Veterans, trade unions, associations, the Association of Socialist Youth ."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that all socio-political organisations are required to get involved in the defence of the country? And then this article, if we can scroll down a little. The rights and duties of socio-political associations or organisations. We know that these are municipalities and republics. We need to see the bottom, lower down. "Rights and duties of socio-political communities," that's the heading; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the heading.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see paragraph 6, sorry, in Article 59. "Organise territorial defence. Ensure the unity of organisation. Control and command. Communications." Article 11: "Preparation of mobilisation." Item 12: "Organise the preparation and training of their organs for work in war and under immediate threat of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that they are able to organise and prepare and enable their organs, and within that framework, they can use the institutions of presidencies, or crisis staffs, or any other way they see fit to make it work?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't see "Crisis Staff" specified, but, yes, the tradition -- the Socialist legislation went on the Partisan tradition and emphasised, well, everybody participating, flexibility, local initiative. In the event of invasion, where you lose contact with the leadership, take local initiative. But this law is referring to the existing legal socio-political units. It expects these duties to be carried out within the existing legal municipalities and other organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this law in force in 1992? And it hasn't been replaced to this day, has it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the current state of -- you mean in -- in the Republic of Bosnia, I mean, I'm sure the laws have been adapted to the present day. I believe this was in force on the 19th of December, 1991, and in the beginning of 1992. I know the RS adopted a lot of the legislation from the former Yugoslavia as its own, but I believe that -- their own Law on Defence, and they certainly did not include the League of Communists' role. I haven't sat down, personally, and done a comparison -- I haven't studied the RS Law on Defence enough to say what is taken from this and what is not, but I'm sure that some things have been changed. I don't know if this system of All People's Defence has been retained. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that until 1995, until the end of the war, this law continued to be in effect without change?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina? I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Republika Srpska proclaimed that the laws it had not adopted, it will adopt and observe from the legislation of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina? The Assembly took that position?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that. I do not know when the RS proclaimed its own Law on Defence and how it compares to this. I simply do not know. But I am certainly aware that, yes, the laws not adopted will be taken from the legislation of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Article 66, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 66 and 67 deal with the role of the Presidency in war and immediate threat of war. The Presidency of Municipal Assembly is organised. The president of a Municipal Assembly directs resistance on the territory of the municipality, and the Presidency must report to the Municipal Assembly as soon as it is able to convene. The Presidency consists of the president and a certain number of members. And it says lower down, on the next page at the top: "President of the Executive Board, Municipal Assembly, president of the Local Board of the League of Communists," that means the ruling party, "Socialist Alliance, commander of the Territorial Defence." Does this Article 67 stipulate the composition of the presidency of a municipal assembly in case of war or immediate threat of war?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see Articles 68 and 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the Municipal Assembly organises a council for national defence? It consists of the president and a certain number of members. Look at Article 68, please, to see what this Council for National Defence deals with: providing direction, funding, All People's Defence, sources of its finance, organising territorial defence, civilian protection, the service of monitoring and alerting, encryption, et cetera. And it says: "In war or immediate threat of war, the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly takes over from the Council." So in war, this Council stops operating, and its role is taken over by the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly. Is it exactly as I read it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this article was translated. When we first saw this document, there was an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we have one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not on my screen, so I didn't know. Yes, the Municipal Assembly shall formulate the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly. It takes over, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that, yes, 68 and 69. Presidency, not Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Municipal Assemble shall form the Council."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then it's the wrong interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He's referring to the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm referring to the first sentence: "The Municipal Assembly shall form the council." The last sentence says that the presidency takes over the functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last sentence says the Presidency takes over the duties; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we look at 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Council consists of the president, a certain number of members, and the president of the Municipal Assembly is, ex officio, president of the Council. Ms. Hanson, maybe I'm not so found of our laws, myself, but you see that a municipality is a state, in a nutshell. It has its president, its commanders, and all the other posts.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Under the former Yugoslav system of self-management, the municipals -- the municipalities had a great deal of autonomy, and here we see, yes, their own commanders, the president of the Municipal Assembly, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see Article 80 to see what the duties and responsibilities of the republic were. "The republic ...," Article 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you cast a glance? It regulates the system of All People's Defence; regulates special rights and duties of working people and citizens; establishes the main elements of assessing the level of threat; plans the work of state authorities, and the work of state authorities is regulated differently in times of war. Was this the basis for forming a Crisis Staff in Bosnia and Herzegovina without declaring a state of war or immediate threat of war?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Crisis Staff of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd have to see that decision again to see if they cite Article 80, specifically, as the basis, but certainly the thrust of the law gives them that kind of authority. But, again, the law does not use the term "crisis staffs," but it gives them, I guess, a great deal of initiative to -- yeah, the organisation of work of state organs. It's a little difficult, I'm sorry, to read this legal Serbian so quickly and absorb it all. But it seems to be in accordance with the law, if not directly based on this law.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see Articles 84 and 85 to see what the Presidency of the Republic is doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "The Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina organises and directs All People's Defence in war as well as all forms of general resistance in the territory of the republic, in keeping with the unity of armed struggle and general defence effort in the country." And then: "The Presidency of the SR BH, in war or in the event of immediate threat of war, at the proposal of the Executive Council ..." Can we see the next column: "... or at its own initiative, shall enact decrees, with the force of law, on issues pertaining to the jurisdiction of the Assembly. If the relevant councils are unable convene, the Presidency of the SR BH shall submit these decrees for ratification to the Assembly as soon as it is able to convene."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the Presidency of the Republika Srpska doing the same thing as envisaged in Articles 84 and 85? I did ask the question, but it was not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we do see the Assembly of the Serb People meeting, so it was able to meet some of the time, at least. But the Presidency of Republika Srpska was, I would say, following the general guide-lines of these laws. I'm not a legal expert to sit down and compare these provisions to actual acts of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 104, please, 104.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The Committee for All People's Defence and Social Self-Protection of the Republic consists of the president and a certain number of members. The president of the Central Committee of the League of Communists of Bosnia-Herzegovina is, ex officio, president of the Committee for All People's Defence and Social Self-Protection of the Republic." Is he performing this role by virtue of the fact that the League of Communists is in power?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the one-party state, it was quite clear which party was in power. So the president of the Central Committee is, ex officio -- the president of the Central Committee of the League of Communists is, ex officio, president of this committee, because it was essentially a one-party state.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at Article 109. It's on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "In the area of two or more municipalities, regional staffs of territorial defence shall be formed and be responsible for organising and preparing units and staffs of territorial defence in the area of these municipalities." Do you agree that municipalities have the right and duty to join forces in order to build up their defence capability?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the legal municipalities have that right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 120, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say that commanders of territorial defence and commanders of units and institutions of territorial defence, in exercising rights and duties from their purview, may adopt -- may issue orders, instructions, rule books, compulsory instructions, and other documents of control and command?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "The commander of the territorial defence of the republic." And, yes, Bosnia, as a republic, had a territorial defence structure. And, yes, it says that it has the right to do these things that you say, that are listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were interpreting Article 121, but please look at Article 120. The same rights belong to commanders and commanding officers of units?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the Territorial Defence. Yes, commanders and officers of the units of the Territorial Defence have those rights and duties.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see Article 207.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 207 speaks of: "Evacuation in war or in the event of immediate threat of war and other emergencies, evacuation of people and property may be organised and conducted from cities and other affected areas, in keeping with the defence plan of the republic. Municipalities, in keeping with the assessed level of risk, may determine that populations should be evacuated." Do you see that this is grounds -- this is a basis for evacuating population at risk?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Municipalities, in accordance with the republic -- defence plan of the republic, can evacuate population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Municipalities, in keeping with their own estimate, their estimate of the level of risk?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, municipalities can make their own estimate of the level of risk and evacuate -- evacuate population from the threatened parts of the municipal territory.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see Article --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this law has punitive provisions? This law stipulates the existence of courts of honour and other sanctions. Can we see Article 402.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know -- I'm not specifically familiar with the punitive provision. I'm not surprised to learn that the law has such provisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you study the whole law - you've read it now - as a basis for conducting war?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not read the entire law.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So beginning with Article 402, until the end, are punitive provisions for certain actions and omissions. Can we see Article 124 to see that there also existed courts of honour. Sorry, Article 324.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say "courts of honour," and several articles govern these courts of honour, beginning with 324 until 325, that these articles govern the courts of honour? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that it says that here. I don't think I read this section in detail. I think I was just looking for sections relative to municipalities, but I see it here now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, in one paragraph, paragraph 147, you say the Presidency was mixed up in the movements of population. Except in the evacuation of population from Vecici village, do you have evidence that the president, or the Presidency, or the government at the central level, was involved in any evacuation or any expulsion of the population? Do you have evidence, a document, to prove that, or does your Article 147 refer only to the case of Kotor Varos, because you connect this paragraph to Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That quotation that I cite certainly applies only to Kotor Varos. I -- that is the only explicit reference I have to the Presidency being involved. The other involvement is through the links -- the reporting, the links from the municipal to the republic level, and in reverse, via the commissioners, and other orders and other documents we see, but that is -- that quotation there refers only to Kotor Varos and only to the case of Vecici.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I can see the clock. If I cannot get any more time on Friday, I have to thank the witness, but I'm asking you again to give me the whole day of Friday, or at least one session. We must note, again with regret, that several expert witnesses of the Prosecution remained unexamined. And I would also like to have this law translated in its entirety and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, on an exceptional basis, the Chamber has decided to give you one hour more on Friday. And we'll admit this, but we'll mark this for identification, pending translation. Ms. Sutherland, you agree that this document has to be translated in its entirety, the law?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have just said the articles that Dr. Karadzic -- Mr. Karadzic took the witness to. But it depends. We'll add up how many they are, and if it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's about 45 -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Then we might as well get the whole document translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we admit it in its entirety, and let's have it be translated. We give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D1359. And, for the record, 65 ter 03719 will be D1358, and not D1351.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Tomorrow, we are not sitting because of the plenary. So, Ms. Hanson, as usual, please do not make any contact with any other people or to discuss about your evidence. Friday, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you for the additional time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 17th day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
